concepts.name: Circular Economy: Definition, Principles and Distinction from Linear Economy
key_dimensions: 3R vs 6R vs 9R framework hierarchy (Refuse, Rethink, Reduce, Reuse, Repair, Refurbish, Remanufacture, Repurpose, Recycle) — order and priority matter
Distinction from linear 'take-make-dispose' model and the intermediate 'recycling economy'
Ellen MacArthur Foundation's definition vs. cradle-to-cradle design philosophy
UPSC trap: Circular economy is NOT simply about recycling — it prioritizes waste prevention over end-of-pipe recycling

concepts.name: Biological vs. Technical Cycles in Circular Economy
key_dimensions: Biological cycle: organic materials returned safely to biosphere through composting/anaerobic digestion
Technical cycle: finite materials (metals, plastics, synthetics) kept in use through reuse, repair, remanufacturing
UPSC trap: Not all materials belong to both cycles — conflating them is a common error
Policy implications: different regulatory frameworks needed for each cycle (EPR for technical; waste-to-energy debate for biological)

concepts.name: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR): Framework and Indian Implementation
key_dimensions: EPR under Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016 (amended 2021, 2022) — mandatory targets, EPR certificates, centralized portal
EPR under E-Waste Management Rules 2022 — Producer Responsibility Organisations (PROs), channelization targets
Distinction: EPR is a policy instrument operationalizing circular economy — UPSC often tests which rules govern which waste stream
Gaps and criticism: informal sector exclusion, certificate trading without actual recycling, lack of traceability

concepts.name: India's Plastic Waste Management Framework and Circular Economy Linkages
key_dimensions: Single-Use Plastic (SUP) ban 2022 — 19 specific items banned; distinction from other plastics not banned
UPSC trap: Not all single-use plastics are banned — only those with 'low utility and high littering potential' per notification
Extended EPR for plastic packaging — four categories: rigid, flexible, multi-layered plastic (MLP), plastic carry bags
India Plastics Pact and voluntary commitments vs. regulatory mandates — overlap and distinction

concepts.name: E-Waste Management: Circular Economy Application to Electronics
key_dimensions: E-Waste Management Rules 2022 — key changes from 2016 rules: inclusion of all producers, PROs, deposit refund scheme provision
Urban mining concept: India is 3rd largest e-waste generator globally — recoverable value of precious metals
Informal sector paradox: handles ~95% of e-waste but uses hazardous methods — formalization challenge
UPSC trap: E-waste rules cover 'electrical and electronic equipment' — solar panels and batteries now separately covered under different rules

concepts.name: Biomimicry and Cradle-to-Cradle (C2C) Design as Circular Economy Enablers
key_dimensions: Cradle-to-Cradle (William McDonough & Michael Braungart) vs. cradle-to-grave: product as nutrient, not waste
Biomimicry: designing systems modeled on natural circular processes — distinct from C2C but complementary
Industrial symbiosis (Kalundborg model): waste of one industry = input for another — geographic clustering requirement
UPSC trap: Industrial symbiosis is a circular economy strategy but operates at ecosystem/industrial park level, not product level

concepts.name: Industrial Symbiosis and Eco-Industrial Parks (EIPs) in India
key_dimensions: NIEPA (National Industrial Symbiosis Programme) — UK origin, adopted in India's MSME context
Eco-Industrial Parks under National Resource Efficiency Policy (NREP) 2019 — distinction from Special Economic Zones
UPSC trap: EIPs are NOT the same as SEZs or smart industrial corridors — specific focus on resource loops
Examples: Naroda Industrial Estate (Ahmedabad), Parwanoo cluster — common energy/water/waste sharing

concepts.name: National Resource Efficiency Policy (NREP) 2019 and Resource Efficiency Framework
key_dimensions: NREP 2019: first dedicated policy — 6 key areas including material recycling, responsible consumption, EIPs
Resource Efficiency Cell under MoEFCC — coordination with NITI Aayog, Ministry of Mines
India Resource Panel (InRP) — advisory body modeled on International Resource Panel (IRP/UNEP)
UPSC trap: NREP is a policy, NOT a law — no statutory backing yet, enforcement limitation is a standard critique

concepts.name: Waste-to-Energy (WtE): Role, Limitations, and Circular Economy Compatibility
key_dimensions: WtE hierarchy position: above landfilling but BELOW reuse, repair, recycling — often misrepresented as circular
Solid Waste Management Rules 2016 mandate WtE for non-recyclable, non-biodegradable waste with calorific value >1500 kcal/kg
UPSC trap: WtE is NOT a circular economy solution — it destroys material value; it is a linear end-of-pipe tool used as a last resort
Conflict with informal waste pickers (ragpickers) — diversion of recyclable waste to WtE plants undermines their livelihoods

concepts.name: Circular Economy in Construction and Demolition (C&D) Waste
key_dimensions: C&D Waste Management Rules 2016 — applies to bulk generators (>20 tonnes/day); processing facility mandate
India generates ~530 million tonnes C&D waste/year — largest waste stream by volume, yet lowest recovery rate
Circular strategies: design for disassembly, use of recycled aggregates in road construction (MORTH guidelines)
UPSC trap: C&D rules apply to 'bulk generators' only — household-level demolition waste largely unregulated

concepts.name: Battery Waste Management and Circular Economy: EV Battery Focus
key_dimensions: Battery Waste Management Rules 2022 — supersedes Batteries (Management & Handling) Rules 2001; covers all battery types including EV batteries
EPR obligations for EV battery producers — collection targets, recycling targets, second-life applications
Second-life batteries concept: repurposing EV batteries for stationary energy storage before recycling
UPSC trap: Battery Waste Management Rules 2022 are separate from E-Waste Rules 2022 — batteries explicitly excluded from e-waste rules

concepts.name: Circular Economy and Textile/Fashion Industry
key_dimensions: Textile sector is 2nd largest polluter globally — fast fashion vs. slow fashion as circular economy dimensions
Takeback schemes, fibre-to-fibre recycling, upcycling — technical vs. biological cycle applicability
India's context: large khadi/handloom sector as a traditional circular model; Jute as a circular material
UPSC trap: India has no dedicated textile waste management rules yet — gap in regulatory framework is an important critique point

concepts.name: Circular Bioeconomy: Integrating Biological Resources into Circular Loops
key_dimensions: Bioeconomy vs. circular economy — bioeconomy uses biological resources; circular bioeconomy applies circular principles to bio-based systems
Applications: bioplastics, bio-based chemicals, biorefineries — distinction from conventional petrochemical value chains
India's National Bioeconomy Policy 2022 — alignment with circular economy goals
UPSC trap: Bioplastics are NOT automatically biodegradable — compostable vs. biodegradable vs. bio-based are three different attributes

concepts.name: Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM) and Urban Solid Waste: Circular Economy Alignment
key_dimensions: SBM Urban 2.0 (2021-26) — focus on source segregation, material recovery facilities (MRFs), legacy waste remediation
Distinction: SBM is primarily a cleanliness/sanitation mission; circular economy framing was added in 2.0 phase
UPSC trap: SBM 2.0 targets 'garbage-free cities' (star ratings 1-7) — NOT the same as zero-waste cities; rating criteria differ
Dry waste collection centres (DWCCs) and their role as nodes in urban circular economy — link to informal sector integration

concepts.name: Global Plastic Treaty (INC Process) and Circular Economy Implications for India
key_dimensions: UNEA Resolution 5/14 (2022): mandate for legally binding global plastics treaty by 2024 — INC 1-5 negotiations
Key fault lines: full life-cycle approach (production caps) vs. waste management-only approach — India's negotiating position
UPSC trap: India supports 'waste management approach' — has NOT endorsed production caps on virgin plastic; nuanced position often misread
Implications for India's petrochemical industry, EPR framework, and plastic waste export regulations (Basel Convention linkage)

concepts.name: Circular Economy Metrics: Material Flow Analysis (MFA) and Circularity Rate
key_dimensions: Circularity rate (circular material use rate): share of recycled materials in total material input — EU measures ~12%, global average ~7.2%
Material Flow Analysis (MFA) as a tool to map resource inputs, stocks, flows, and waste outputs in an economy
Domestic Material Consumption (DMC) vs. Material Footprint — DMC undercounts hidden flows and imports
UPSC trap: Higher recycling rate does NOT equal higher circularity — circularity also requires reduction and reuse upstream; recycling-only focus is a systemic error

concepts.name: Right to Repair Movement and Product Longevity as Circular Economy Strategy
key_dimensions: Right to Repair framework (India): Committee constituted 2022 under DPIIT — covers mobiles, consumer electronics, farming equipment, automobiles
EU Right to Repair Directive 2024 — manufacturer obligations to provide spare parts, repair manuals for 10 years
UPSC trap: Right to Repair is NOT yet a statutory right in India — currently a framework/guideline, not legislation
Conflict with planned obsolescence business model — regulatory vs. market-based approaches to product longevity

concepts.name: Circular Economy and Critical Minerals: Recycling vs. Virgin Extraction
key_dimensions: Critical minerals (lithium, cobalt, nickel, REEs) are essential for clean energy transition but pose supply chain risks
Circular strategies: urban mining, battery recycling, product design for mineral recovery — reduces primary extraction dependency
India's Critical Mineral Mission 2023 and National Critical Mineral Strategy — recycling component vs. overseas acquisition focus
UPSC trap: Critical Minerals Amendment to MMDR Act 2023 focuses on exploration/mining — recycling/secondary recovery is a separate policy gap not addressed by the amendment

concepts.name: Informal Waste Economy: Ragpickers, Kabadiwallas and Circular Economy Integration
key_dimensions: India's informal waste sector recovers ~20-25% of recyclables — often more efficient than formal systems at lower cost
Integration challenges: social stigma, lack of legal recognition, health risks, displacement by mechanized systems
Successful models: SWaCH cooperative (Pune), Hasiru Dala (Bengaluru) — formal integration with municipal systems
UPSC trap: Informal sector is a de facto circular economy actor but is excluded from EPR certificate systems — a critical policy gap and social justice issue simultaneously

concepts.name: Circular Economy Finance: Green Bonds, Blended Finance and Circular Business Models
key_dimensions: Circular business models: product-as-a-service (PaaS), performance economy, sharing platforms — shift from ownership to access
SEBI's Green Bond framework and RBI's green deposit framework — do they explicitly cover circular economy projects?
UPSC trap: Green bonds in India are governed by SEBI's Green Bond framework (2023) — 'circular economy' is listed as an eligible green category but verification/certification is self-declared
Blended finance for circular economy MSMEs — SIDBI's initiatives, UNEP-aligned instruments for emerging economies
